summary: On the second day of Sam Bankman-Fried's fraud trial, a jury was selected and prosecutors and defense lawyers gave opening statements presenting opposing portraits of the former FTX CEO. The government called him a man who lied and stole billions, while his lawyer called him a good-faith startup founder. The first witnesses were FTX customer Marc-Antoine Julliard and Bankman-Fried's MIT friend Adam Yedidia.
one_line: Opening statements in Sam Bankman-Fried's trial pit prosecutors' claim of billions stolen against the defense's good-faith founder story, before first witnesses testify.
key_facts: The jury in Sam Bankman-Fried's trial was selected on Wednesday morning, the second day of the trial, before opening statements.
Prosecutor Thane Rehn said in his roughly 30-minute opening that "all of that, all of it, was built on lies" and that Bankman-Fried "stole billions of dollars from thousands of victims."
The government alleges Bankman-Fried used Alameda Research, with Caroline Ellison as a front, to get "secret access" to customer cash and crypto.
Prosecutors allege he directed employees to conceal money flowing into FTX and forged financial documents given to lenders and investors.
Defense lawyer Mark Cohen said "Sam didn't defraud anyone" and described him as a nerdy founder acting in "good faith," not a "cartoon of a villain."
Cohen argued Alameda acted legally as an FTX customer, payment processor and market maker, and said "working at a startup is like building a plane as you're flying it."
Cohen pointed the finger at Ellison, saying she did not adequately protect Alameda from crypto market risk.
Bankman-Fried had spent about seven weeks in a Brooklyn prison before the trial.
The first witness, Marc-Antoine Julliard, a Paris-born cocoa trader living in London, tried on Nov. 8 to withdraw almost $100,000 from FTX and was "never" able to.
Adam Yedidia, a Bankman-Fried friend from MIT who worked at Alameda and then FTX, testified with immunity, saying "I was concerned that I had unwittingly written code that contributed to a crime."
Court adjourned near 4:30 p.m.; Yedidia continues Thursday, followed by Matt Huang of Sequoia Capital and then Gary Wang.
Attendees included Bankman-Fried's parents and Damian Williams, U.S. attorney for the Southern District of New York.
